# Native local-speech client evidence

The immutable reference is Mluva v1.6.0 at `5202477edfe4b5d8bacfa5b2e9fd6eadd9624f7f`. The ignored collector verifies all twelve imported application/resource files against that commit before calling the unchanged public local-speech factory. Maintained production code and checks use Rust; reference collection stays outside the maintained tree.

`released-local-asr.json` records 230 independent sessions, 192 requests, 186 worker starts and 170 successful results. SHA-256: `edbd3c4229b61319160a024dd4578853707570c291a52941c477b84833f89148`. Both clients own real isolated child processes. A controlled native peer supplies protocol replies, and sparse model/runtime files satisfy their readiness checks; this table does not perform speech inference. Normalization removes owned root paths, process IDs and the interpreter-specific launch prefix. Native CUDA library/cache fields are checked separately; the common inherited environment, model/path/device arguments, null diagnostics, exact request-body hashes, result metadata and process lifetimes match the release.

Both retained ONNX models exercise every released language code and ISO alias, automatic/empty/unknown values, Parakeet's unsupported-language diagnostic and preflight ordering. Missing/incomplete/wrong-size model files, absent GPU support, invalid executables, startup exit, malformed replies and failure/restart preserve controlled errors. Unicode and resolved/symlink/missing audio paths preserve request bytes. Retained workers survive unsupported-language preflight failures; ordinary request errors close them. ONNX emits no provisional callback and returns the originally requested language code, null probability/ID/duration and empty speaker segments. The public factory also selects the Qwen-specific missing-model diagnostic.

Eight failing response controls demonstrated the owning repairs: unused NaN/infinite metadata, complete JSON at EOF, CR at EOF, both valid ASCII boundary lengths and multibyte character limits. The native reader now normalizes CR/LF, counts decoded Unicode characters up to the released 2,000,001-character limit, accepts complete JSON without a trailing newline and preserves duplicate-text last-value behavior. Nonfinite values are tolerated only as non-string JSON values; literal strings remain unchanged, and required text must be a string. Invalid UTF-8, trailing garbage and malformed text still fail. The native deadline covers the complete reply; the released selector stops its deadline once the first byte becomes readable. No claim is made that the native client reproduces that legacy indefinite-read failure.

Closing during delayed loading and cancelling active work observe prompt child reaping with no late successful result. The released `close()` can leave its active selector waiting after the child is reaped; the collector cancels that isolated client only as cleanup after recording close latency. The native owner wakes its pending request immediately. Cancellation's racy interpreter error text is normalized to interruption/no-output and cleanup rather than copied into the native API. A separate four-route native check drops the request future without calling close, observes the CPU/CUDA worker and private shader cache disappear, then starts a successful new capture. It failed before repair because the next capture reused the dead session. Both concurrent cancel callers now return only after all owned resources are gone.

`released-local-asr-faults.json` freezes four additional independent released sessions. SHA-256: `6ecf4e707f2107edd81848b8038f3d9a650cc946f077617dc40d55c4d1f013f7`. Two explicitly executed ignored native checks match actual CPU/CUDA 180-second silent-worker deadlines and actual resident-memory overflow above 5 GB, including exact errors, process disappearance and cache cleanup. An additional native partial-JSON case proves the same elapsed complete-reply deadline; its timeout deliberately avoids the release's selector/readline hang instead of claiming partial-reply parity. The memory peer really allocates/touches 5.1 GB, one worker at a time; the harness requires at least 12 GB available. These are real elapsed-time/RSS guards against controlled workers, not excessive-memory inference or physical GPU proofs. Production constants, clocks and `/proc` data are not replaced by test controls.

The two opt-in [physical ONNX comparisons](../../../mluva-asr/tests/fixtures/README.md) now call the same public native factory instead of sending worker JSONL directly. All sixteen frozen released CPU/CUDA results and metadata match, with four further cold-restart comparisons. External `/proc` observations prove retained/restarted workers and reaping; external NVIDIA telemetry proves each CUDA worker has nonzero GPU memory. Cancelling actual model loading returns within the check's two-second bound with no result and no remaining worker/cache. The unchanged [Qwen inference evidence](qwen-inference-evidence.md) separately covers the default model's CPU/NVIDIA recognitions and provisional callbacks.

```sh
cargo test --locked -p mluva-providers --test local_asr
cargo test --locked -p mluva-providers --test local_asr \
  actual_worker_deadlines_match_release_and_close_every_owned_resource \
  -- --ignored --exact
cargo test --locked -p mluva-providers --test local_asr \
  actual_resident_overflow_matches_released_guard_and_reaps_owned_workers \
  -- --ignored --exact
```

The controlled peer's parent-death signal protects fixture processes only; it is not production crash evidence. Non-object replies use controlled native failures instead of the legacy unchecked attribute error. Arbitrary nonstandard JSON, non-UTF-8 filesystem paths, broader real languages/audio, malformed/empty WAV worker behavior, production app-crash cleanup, complete controller/UI/Live workflows, distribution and performance measurements remain required acceptance work. Qwen's separate full startup/stream deadlines and resident overflow still need explicit acceptance. No microphone, host cache, managed credential, user-content upload or visible desktop input was used. The installed app/widget remain v1.6.0 and full application parity is not claimed.
